newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims up in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims up in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits jumped last week, the government said Thursday.
In its weekly jobless claims report, the Labour Department said new filings climbed to 366,000 in the week ended Dec. 28, up from a revised 344,000 in the previous week.
The department previously reported 335,000 claims in the week ended Dec. 21.

The four-week moving average, considered a more accurate gauge of employment trends because it smooths out weekly fluctuations, also rose last week. It stood at 352,500, up from a revised 343,500 in the earlier week.
Total benefit rolls swelled to 2,558,000 in the week ended Dec. 21, the most recent week for which those figures were available. Total claims stood at 2,456,000 the previous week.
The department said initial claims of 366,000 in the week ended Dec. 28 were the highest since the July 13 week, when they reached 367,000.
The department said 17 states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Dec. 21, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Virginia, with 6,661 additional jobless claims, Kentucky with 5,201, Texas with 4,108, Illinois with 4,030, Missouri with 3,341 and Indiana with 3,168.
Virginia reported layoffs in the textile, apparel, food and primary metals industries. Kentucky had layoffs in the glass and electrical equipment industries.
In Illinois and Missouri there were layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries. Missouri also had layoffs in the glass industry and Illinois in manufacturing.

Indiana reported layoffs in the rubber, lumber, transportation equipment, fabricated metals, electrical equipment and non-electrical machinery industries. Texas provided no reason for its increase in claims.
Labour said five states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Dec. 21 week.
They were California, with 10,680 fewer filings, North Carolina with 7,003, Georgia with 3,064, South Carolina with 2,649 and Alabama with 1,544.
California said it had fewer layoffs in the construction industry and in agriculture, while North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the textile, furniture and electrical equipment industries.
Alabama had fewer layoffs in the textile, apparel and service industries. Georgia and South Carolina had no comment.
